security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD kernel accesses user memory (copyin/copyout, signal frame setup, ptrace, core dump) without byte-swapping when the current process has sstatus.UBE=1, OR the context-switch path fails to save/restore sstatus.UBE, leaking endianness state between processes.
security_spec.summary: FreeBSD is little-endian; if a process enables big-endian U-mode via sstatus.UBE (Ssube), all kernel-user data boundaries—copyin/copyout, signal frames, ptrace, coredumps, and context switches—become endianness-mismatch surfaces that the kernel has no code to handle, silently corrupting process data.

findings.finding: No SSTATUS_UBE macro defined. Bits skip from SPIE(5) to SPP(8). UBE(bit 6) is completely absent from the kernel's register-definition layer.

spec_citations.excerpt: UBE controls whether explicit load and store memory accesses made from U-mode are little-endian (UBE=0) or big-endian (UBE=1).

findings.finding: All copyin/copyout paths use native S-mode loads/stores (lb/sb/ld/sd) without byte-swapping. No defense-in-depth against a future code path that might allow UBE=1.
memset(tf,0,sizeof(*tf)) implicitly clears UBE=0 on exec. Every new binary starts in LE mode.
UBE (bit 6) is NOT in the ignore-mask for sstatus validation. Any sigreturn/setcontext attempt to change UBE is rejected with EINVAL.
Full sstatus saved/restored round-trip through traps (csrr→sd→...→ld→csrw). UBE preserved intact.
findings.snippet:
csrr	t0, sstatus
sd	t0, (TF_SSTATUS)(sp)
/* ... */
csrw	sstatus, t0

findings.finding: sstatus managed through trapframe (TD_FRAME), not directly in cpu_switch. Per-thread sstatus correctly persists across context switches.
findings.snippet:
/* cpu_switch saves ra, sp, s0-s11 only */
/* sstatus lives in trapframe, managed at trap boundaries */

findings.finding: Child inherits parent's trapframe (UBE=0 since kernel never allows UBE=1). SPIE set and SPP cleared for user-mode entry.
Guest sstatus initialized with UBE=0. Full sstatus virtualized through csrrw save/restore in vmm_switch.S.
Signal delivery captures full sstatus via get_mcontext, copyout's in LE format (matching UBE=0). Sigreturn validated by set_mcontext which rejects UBE changes.
ptrace fill_regs reads sstatus; set_regs does NOT write sstatus back. Debugger can read but not modify UBE through ptrace.
findings.snippet:
/* fill_regs: */ regs->sstatus = frame->tf_sstatus;
/* set_regs: sstatus NOT written back */

findings.finding: Forked process restores full sstatus from trapframe (UBE=0 given exec_setregs or fork_inherit). Only SIE masked before sret.
findings.snippet:
ld	t0, (TF_SSTATUS)(sp)
li	t1, ~SSTATUS_SIE
and	t0, t0, t1
csrw	sstatus, t0
